title: Purge Protocol
mood: Something vast comes through the sky over the bay, and Guinevere spends everything she has left.

hero.alt: Seen from high above, a city of dark towers lies broken and burning under smoke.

segs.t: Lesley stood behind Chang’e’s chair, one hand on its back, her rifle on her shoulder.
On the feed, Guinevere stood alone on the lower platform. Across from her stood a woman in a long robe, with Enders at her back.
Voices came over the open channel, one on top of another.
“That’s Vexana.”
“Her hair’s different.”
“It’s her. She’s with them.”
“Traitor.”
The word came first from the hall, where the students stood packed under the big display. Then from the waterfront. It went down the channel faster than any order.
Chang’e had stopped typing. “Look at this.”

Down one side of her console ran a column of thin lines. Every suit in the city sent its power to the deck, one line each. The suits ran on belief, so those lines were as close as anyone could come to reading it.
They were falling. All of them at once, frontline and rear.
“Nobody’s been hit,” said Chang’e. “It isn’t damage. It’s them.”
“It’s working on us,” she said.
“What is?”
“Her face.”
She had stood on enough walls to know it.
Show a line its best fighter on the other side,
she thought,
and the line stops believing it can win. You don’t have to shoot a suit that runs on belief.
The morning list sat in the corner of Chang’e’s screen. Beside Vexana’s name was one word. Lesley had entered it herself every morning since the capture.
“Her file,” said Chang’e. “It says Missing.”
A file says what I can prove,
thought Lesley.
“It stays Missing.”
A voice cut in on the channel. “Wall guns, west ward. We have the woman on the platform. Permission to fire.”
“Hold,” said Lesley. “Guinevere is on that platform. Nobody fires on it.”
“Holding.”
Then the big slow line from that morning, the one VOID NOTES had matched, went off the top of the scale.
Chang’e’s hands came off the keys. “It’s here.”
On the feed, over the platforms, the sky tore open into a star.
The platforms.
The wind dragged Guinevere toward the tear.
A hand came out of the star first.
It was huge and clawed, plated in violet. Its fingers hooked over the edge of the sky. Then a head pushed through, horned and crowned with spikes. Then wings, each one as wide as a ward.
Only half of it was through. That half already filled the sky over the bay.

media.alt: A star-shaped tear burns open in a violet sky over the city; a huge clawed hand pushes out of it; then a horned, crowned head and vast glowing wings push through.

segs.t: She had heard of it once, in Teacher Chang’e’s class. The Will of the Planet sent the Enders, and the readings suggested it had a body. Teacher Chang’e called that body the Mother Matrix. Nobody had ever seen it.
Guinevere was seeing it now.
The voice came from everywhere at once.
“The gateway is near completion. Soon, you Aspirants will meet your end.”
Guinevere looked at Vexana.
A breath ago Vexana had stared at the star on Guinevere’s collar with her mouth open, and no word had come. Now her face had gone cold.
“Vexana. Execute purge protocol.”

media.alt: Close on Vexana's face, washed in violet light between two gold stars, her eyes glowing and cold.

segs.t: Purge.
To purge a place was to wipe it clean.
It just told her to kill me,
thought Guinevere.
Vexana swept her staff.

High on the ledges over the platforms, something huge unfolded. A giant Ender dropped out of the smoke with a sword taller than a house, and brought it down. The platform burst. Guinevere leapt back through flying stone.
One more Ender. Her eyes went past Vexana, up to the thing in the sky.
You’ve got her,
she thought.
You’ve got hold of her.
“You... give her back to me!”
Her wings of light opened, and she flew straight at it.
Enders rose to stop her. She went through them, rolled under a claw and came up over a shoulder. Below her the wards slid past, burning. Nearly half the city was already rubble.
A violet shot came up from below, from where Vexana stood.
It took her in the side and drove her through the wall of a tower.
She lay in glass and broken stone, and the ringing came back into her ears. She climbed out over the rubble with blood at her lip.

media.alt: A giant armored figure drops out of the sky and smashes down in a burst of violet light; Guinevere flies low through the towers and over a dark Ender; below, Vexana fires her staff; Guinevere is driven through a tower and crashes into the rubble.

segs.t: Vexana had come after her. She stood on a broken ledge above, the staff low.
“Give up, Guinevere. Hope is an illusion. Its ‘Will’ is absolute.”
Guinevere wiped her mouth on her wrist.
“I refuse.”
Her drones came back to her shoulders slowly. They hung a hand lower than they should, and their yellow eyes had gone dull. Her power was running low.
A great lady does not land early.
Vexana raised the staff. The three giants rose out of the smoke around her, swords dragging sparks. Guinevere came on anyway. She went under the first sword and over the second.
Wings opened on both of them, wings of aspirant power. They rose at each other across the broken air.

media.alt: Guinevere rises over the ruined platforms on a tall wing of red and gold light, her two drones blazing beside her.

segs.t: The arrow had taken some of her. The great spell had taken more, and the tower wall more again. She put everything that was left into her wings and drove at Vexana.
Reach her.
Light burst white and gold between them and took everything.
She was falling.
Her wings had gone out. One drone tumbled past her, dark. Her arms would not lift. Under her the platforms had split, and the gap went all the way down to the bay.

media.alt: Under a shaft of pale light, Guinevere falls headfirst between the towers of the city, her pink hair streaming below her.

segs.t: Vexana is there,
she thought, the way she always had. She waited for the hand on her wrist.
The noise of the fight went somewhere far off. It was very quiet.
She knew this quiet. Her room at night, when she was small. Hester’s footsteps going away down the corridor. Stopping. Then the long, still wait before they came back.
Above her, Vexana hung in the white with her wings still open. Small. Getting smaller.
Stop,
thought Guinevere.
Come back.
The day of the badges. Vexana reaching over without a word to straighten her crooked bow. Then their two hands clasped while the whole hall cheered.
Tears ran back from the corners of her eyes into her hair.
It took everything she had left to get one hand up, toward the figure above. On the arm guard, the little black-haired Vexana swung on its clip. At her collar the star was still lit.
“Don’t let me be alone in this world,” said Guinevere.
Her hand stayed open in the air.
Then nothing.
The command deck.
The feed went white.
When it cleared, Guinevere was falling. Her point on Chang’e’s map dropped with her into the gap.
Then the point was gone.
“I’ve lost her,” said Chang’e. “Her signal just... stopped.”
On the feed the gap was empty, all the way down to the water.
Where the two of them had met, there was only smoke. The three giants lay still in the rubble under the platforms.
“The woman?” said Lesley.
“Smoke. I can’t find her.”
The channel had gone silent, and the hall with it.
Lesley’s hand had closed on the back of the chair. She did not remember closing it.
I’m here this time,
she thought.
I’m right here. And it’s a screen.
The console chimed.
Her point was back on the map, three streets west of the platforms.
“That’s her suit.” Chang’e stared at it. “She was in the gap. Nothing on the feed carried her out. Unless something did.”
She brought up the ward camera on that street. An empty road. A low wall. Behind it, down at the level of the stones, a small gold glow.
“Her Emblem,” said Lesley.
Out past the deck’s window, over the bay, the crowned head turned slowly toward the west.
“If my readings are right, that’s its body,” said Chang’e. “The Mother Matrix.”
On the feed, white light began to gather behind the plates of its chest.
“It’s aiming at her.” Chang’e’s voice went up. “Big Sis!”
Lesley’s thumb was already on the bolt. Her machine eye laid its teal lines out over the bay and gave her the range. No rifle could cross it.
The plates of its chest split. The Mother Matrix fired.
The beam crossed the city, white, and lit the long window from end to end. On the street camera, something dropped out of the smoke above the road.
It was a machine of purple plate edged in gold. It landed between the wall and the light with its arms up. A magenta heart crest blazed on its chest.
The beam broke over it.
Light poured out across the stone on either side and melted a stripe of the road to glass. Out of the feed’s speaker came a long scream of plate. The machine leaned into the light, and held.
Then the light died.
The channel broke its silence. “West ward. Something took that shot. What is that?”
Chang’e switched to the platforms. Every Ender on them had turned its head toward the west. The woman in the robe was not among them.
“That’s not one of theirs,” said Chang’e, very small.
“No,” said Lesley.
On the console, the lines had stopped falling. Not one of them was climbing yet.
Lesley keyed the rescue team.
“Layla. Guinevere is three streets west of the platforms. Something just took the Matrix’s shot for her. Get to her if you can.”
“Copy,” said Layla, over the roar of her cannon.
On the street camera, the machine was still standing in the smoke, its arms half lowered. Its eyes went dark, one after the other.
